revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Refueling the Lander
revealWordProblem.text: A space-station crew has 27.6 liters of fuel to load into the lander. Each fuel cell holds exactly 3.45 liters. How many fuel cells can the crew completely fill? Make the divisor a whole number first, then divide.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 27.6 ÷ 3.45 = 8 fuel cells. Multiply both numbers by 100 to make the divisor whole: 2760 ÷ 345 = 8. Check: 8 × 3.45 = 27.6 liters.

conceptIntro.heading: How do you divide with decimals?
conceptIntro.intro: Dividing splits a total into equal groups. When you divide by a decimal, you first make the divisor (the number you divide by) a whole number, so the division is easier.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Move the decimal point the same number of places in BOTH the divisor and the dividend; the answer stays the same.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want 18.9 ÷ 6.3. The divisor is 6.3, and I want it to be a whole number.
I move the decimal point 1 place right in the divisor: 6.3 becomes 63.
I must move the dividend the same 1 place right: 18.9 becomes 189. Now the problem is 189 ÷ 63.
I check by multiplying: 6.3 × 3 = 18.9. Correct — 3 pods can be filled.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's do 8.4 ÷ 2.1. How many places do we move to make 2.1 a whole number? (1 place, so 2.1 becomes 21.)
Move the dividend the same way: 8.4 becomes 84. What is the new problem? (84 ÷ 21.)

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next, you will rewrite decimal divisions as whole-number divisions and solve them on your own.
Remember: move the point the same number of places in both numbers.

workedExample.label: Order
workedExample.work: A $13.50 catering tray is split into 0.45-pound scoops. How many scoops?

optional.correctWork: Moving both points 2 places gives 1350 ÷ 45, which equals 30, not 3.0 — the decimal point was placed one spot too far left. So 13.50 ÷ 0.45 = 30 scoops. Check: 30 × 0.45 = 13.50. ✓
hints: After you rewrite it as 1350 ÷ 45, estimate first: about how many 45s fit in 1350? That is much more than 3.
1350 ÷ 45 = 30. The cashier slid the decimal one place too far left, turning 30 into 3.0.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
hints: Dividing by a decimal is awkward — notice the divisor 1.2 has one decimal place. There's a move that makes it whole.
Multiply BOTH numbers by 10: scaling dividend and divisor the same way keeps the quotient exactly the same.
Compute 14.4 × 10 = 144 and 1.2 × 10 = 12. Now solve 144 ÷ 12 — a whole-number division you already know how to do.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
hints: The divisor 0.6 has one decimal place — shifting both numbers one place makes the divisor a whole number.
Multiply both numbers by 10 to build an equivalent problem, then divide, keeping the decimal point in the dividend.
3.78 × 10 = 37.8 and 0.6 × 10 = 6. Now compute 37.8 ÷ 6, keeping the decimal point lined up in your answer.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
hints: Ask yourself: how many groups of 0.7 fit inside 8.4? Since 0.7 is less than 1, expect MORE groups than 8.
Scale both numbers by 10 so you're dividing by a whole number instead of a decimal.
8.4 becomes 84 and 0.7 becomes 7. Solve 84 ÷ 7 — your 7s times-table facts will carry you there.

approaching.label: Rewrite each problem by making the divisor a whole number, then solve.
hints: The 'Multiply Both By' column is the key move: choose 10 or 100 based on how many decimal places the DIVISOR has.
One decimal place in the divisor means multiply both numbers by 10; then rewrite and divide whole numbers.
Row 1: 0.9 has one decimal place, so multiply 4.5 and 0.9 each by 10 and write the new whole-number problem in the row.

choiceFeedback: Re-read the problem carefully and try again.
hints: The divisor 1.3 isn't a whole number — shift both numbers before you divide anything.
Multiply dividend and divisor by 10, then divide. Check at the end: your answer times 1.3 should rebuild 15.6.
15.6 × 10 = 156 and 1.3 × 10 = 13. Now count how many 13s fit into 156 — start by trying 13 × 10.

approaching.title: approaching — Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: The student moved the decimal point in the divisor (0.8 → 8) but forgot to move it the same 1 place in the dividend. You must move BOTH: 6.4 becomes 64, so 64 ÷ 8 = 8. So 6.4 ÷ 0.8 = 8. Check: 8 × 0.8 = 6.4. ✓
hints: When you moved 0.8 to 8, what did you have to do to 6.4 as well?
Move the decimal the same 1 place in both: 6.4 → 64, then 64 ÷ 8 = 8.

onLevel.label: Solve each decimal division problem.
hints: Every row uses the same move: shift both numbers until the divisor is whole, then divide as usual.
Count the divisor's decimal places to pick ×10 or ×100 — a divisor like 0.24 needs ×100 — then divide the new whole numbers.
Row 1: 9.6 ÷ 0.8 becomes 96 ÷ 8 after multiplying both by 10. Solve that, then apply the same shift to every other row.

onLevel.label: Match each decimal division to its quotient.
hints: Shift both numbers in each problem until the divisor is whole — most of these turn into basic division facts.
Estimate sizes too: dividing by a number less than 1 gives a quotient BIGGER than the dividend itself.
Try 7.2 ÷ 0.8: times 10 turns it into 72 ÷ 8, a times-table fact. Match it, then shift each remaining problem the same way.

onLevel.stem: A water tank holds 19.2 liters. It is poured into bottles that each hold 1.6 liters. How many bottles can be filled?
choiceFeedback: Multiply the whole numbers first, then count decimal places.
The digits look right—how many total decimal places should the product have?
hints: You're asking how many 1.6s fit into 19.2 — that's division, and the divisor 1.6 needs to become whole first.
Multiply both amounts by 10 to build an equivalent whole-number division, then divide.
19.2 × 10 = 192 and 1.6 × 10 = 16. Now divide 192 by 16 — start by taking out the chunk 16 × 10 = 160.

onLevel.instructions: Sort: should you multiply both numbers by 10 or by 100 to make the divisor a whole number?
hints: Look ONLY at the divisor — the second number in each problem. Count its decimal places; that count makes the decision.
One decimal place in the divisor (like 0.7 or 2.1) means ×10. Two places (like 0.12 or 0.36) means ×100.
Take '6.3 ÷ 0.7': the divisor 0.7 has one decimal place, so it needs ×10. Place it, then count places on each remaining divisor.

onLevel.title: onLevel — Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Move both decimal points
workedExample.work: 0.12 has 2 decimal places, so move both points 2 places: 9.6 ÷ 0.12 becomes 960 ÷ 12.

workedExample.label: Divide and place the decimal
workedExample.work: 960 ÷ 12 = 80, but the student wrote the answer as 8.0.

onLevel.correctWork: The setup 960 ÷ 12 is correct, but the student misplaced the decimal in the quotient. 960 ÷ 12 = 80, not 8. So 9.6 ÷ 0.12 = 80. Estimate to confirm: 0.12 is tiny, so many of them fit in 9.6 — the quotient must be large. Check: 80 × 0.12 = 9.6. ✓
hints: Estimate first: 0.12 is tiny, so how many of them fit in 9.6 — a small answer like 0.8, or a big one?
Both numbers moved 2 places: 9.6 → 960 and 0.12 → 12, so 960 ÷ 12 = 80. The answer is 80.

extending.title: Find Derek's Mistake
extending.correctWork: Derek only multiplied by 10, but the divisor 0.45 has two decimal places. He should multiply both numbers by 100: 720 ÷ 45 = 16. He got the right answer by luck this time, but his method is unreliable because the divisor is still a decimal (4.5).
hints: How many decimal places does 0.45 have? Did Derek multiply by enough to make it a whole number?
0.45 has two decimal places, so multiply both by 100, not 10. 0.45 × 100 = 45 and 7.2 × 100 = 720.

extending.prompt: A gas station sells fuel at $3.45 per gallon. A customer pays $27.60 total. How many gallons did the customer buy? Set up the decimal division, show how to convert it to whole-number division, and solve.
extending.sentenceFrame: The equation is $27.60 ÷ $3.45 = ___. I multiply both by ___ to get ___ ÷ ___ = ___ gallons.
hints: Total money ÷ price per gallon = gallons, so set up 27.60 ÷ 3.45 — and notice the divisor has TWO decimal places.
Multiply both numbers by 100 so the divisor becomes a whole number, then divide the two new whole numbers.
27.60 × 100 = 2,760 and 3.45 × 100 = 345. Now ask how many 345s fit into 2,760 — note that 345 × 10 = 3,450 is already too big.

extending.instructions: Verify each division by showing that quotient × divisor = dividend. Are the two sides balanced?
hints: A balanced scale says the same thing twice: quotient × divisor must rebuild the dividend exactly.
Multiply out the right side of each scale and compare it to the left side's dividend — any mismatch means unbalanced.
First scale: does 12 × 0.8 really equal 9.6? Compute 12 × 8 = 96, give it one decimal place, and compare with the left side.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Decimals is moving the decimal point in the divisor but forgetting to move it the same number of places in the dividend. For example, in 6.4 ÷ 0.8 a student changes 0.8 to 8 but leaves the dividend as 6.4, then divides 6.4 ÷ 8 = 0.8 instead of moving both points to get 64 ÷ 8 = 8. A second version of this mistake happens when the divisor has two decimal places, like 0.12: students move both points only 1 place instead of 2, turning 9.6 ÷ 0.12 into 96 ÷ 1.2 instead of the correct 960 ÷ 12. Count the divisor's decimal places first, then move BOTH points that same number of places.

choiceFeedback: Move both decimals so you divide by a whole number, then divide.
Check your decimal placement — you shifted one place too many.
Dividing by less than 1 makes the answer larger, not smaller.
hints: Notice the divisor 0.8 has one decimal place — that tells you exactly how far to shift both numbers.
Multiply both 19.2 and 0.8 by 10 to create an equivalent division with a whole-number divisor.
That gives 192 ÷ 8. Break it apart: 160 ÷ 8 = 20, then divide the leftover 32 by 8 and combine your two pieces.
